newsitem.title: GERMANY: More platinum jewellery sold in Germany in 1996.
newsitem.headline: More platinum jewellery sold in Germany in 1996.

text.p: German sales of platinum jewellery in 1996 rose both in value and volume, bucking negative trends in gold and diamonds, a statement from producer-funded promoters Platinum Guild (PGI) said on Monday.
Platinum jewellery sales in 1996 rose by two percent to 467 million marks and sales of jewellery items were up five percent at 279,014, it said.
German platinum consumption in jewellery rose to 1.73 tonnes from 1.70 tonnes in 1995.
PGI said platinum had a 5.2 percent share in total German jewellery items and a 13 percent share of mark-denominated jewellery sales.
Consumers opting for platinum took market share away from gold jewellery as sales of gold jewellery items were down by four percent and sales returns off two percent.
Sales of diamond jewellery items dropped by 13 percent and sales values were down three percent.
PGI did not provide gold and diamonds sales totals.
One particular growth area for platinum were wedding rings, where sales of platinum items improved by 17 percent compared with a 12 percent increase in the equivalent gold products.
Jewellery accounts for some 35 percent of the world's platinum consumption, with the rest made up of autocatalysts, chemical, electronic and mineral oil industries.
Platin Gilde International (Deutschland) GmbH, is part of the international PGI group, which also operates in Japan, Italy and the U.S..
It is sponsored by South African producer Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd.
